data.one_liner: Detects whether an Android or iOS device is currently in the lock screen state.
data.what_it_does: Provides a method to check if the device is locked using platform-specific APIs on Android and a heuristic combining protected data and screen brightness on iOS. It helps determine whether the app entered the background because the user locked the screen or left the app.
use_when: You need to know if the app went to the background because the user locked the device screen.
You want to handle app lifecycle changes differently depending on whether the device is locked.
avoid_when: You require a bulletproof, 100% reliable security source of truth on iOS, as iOS detection relies on a heuristic.
You are running tests on an iOS simulator, since it only works on physical devices for iOS.
strengths: Distinguishes between app minimization and screen locking.
Provides both a nullable API and a throwing API for handling errors.
Uses safe native APIs instead of private APIs that violate App Store guidelines.
weaknesses: iOS implementation is purely heuristic and does not use a stable public lock-screen API.
Does not work on iOS simulators (physical device required).
